newsitem.title: USA: N.J. ends special tax regime for regulated utils..
newsitem.headline: N.J. ends special tax regime for regulated utils..

text.p: Gov. Christie Whitman Monday ended a 100-year-old special tax regime for regulated utilities, putting them on the same footing as other corporations.

The law eliminates the gross receipts and franchise tax. which for nearly a century exempted regulated utilities -- including transit, water and energy providers -- from local property taxes. In return they added 13 percent to the basic rates.

But with transit companies now under a state corporation and energy utilities under increasing competition from unregulated sources, the Whitman administration proposed ending the tax. The unregulated companies pay a six-percent sales tax and corporate income taxes on profits, a tariff burden that gives them a competitive edge.
A secondary issue was the loss of revenue to the state's local governments.
A second bill guarantees that at least $730 million would be distributed to the state's 567 municipalities. That figure is the average of recent GRAFT distributions.
